subject: Engineering Mathematics
summary: gradient, directional derivatives and normals, divergence and curl, irrotational and conservative fields, line integrals and work, and the Green, Gauss (divergence) and Stokes theorems

questions.text: The magnitude of the gradient of φ = x²y + yz³ at the point (1, 2, 1) (round off to two decimal places) is ______
solution: Concept: ∇φ = (∂φ/∂x, ∂φ/∂y, ∂φ/∂z); its magnitude is the maximum rate of change of φ.
Exam tip: ∇φ points along the normal to the level surface φ = constant through the point.

questions.text: The directional derivative of φ = x² + 2y² + 3z² at the point (1, 1, 1) in the direction of the vector i + 2j + 2k (round off to two decimal places) is ______
solution: Concept: Directional derivative = ∇φ · â, where â is the unit vector of the given direction.
Exam tip: Forgetting to normalise the direction is the most common mistake: (2, 4, 6)·(1, 2, 2) = 22 is wrong by a factor of 3.

questions.text: The unit normal to the surface x² + y² − z = 1 at the point (1, 1, 1) is
solution: Concept: For a surface f(x, y, z) = c, the normal is ∇f.
Unit normal = (2i + 2j − k)/3 (or its negative)
Exam tip: The angle between two surfaces at a common point is the angle between their gradient vectors.

questions.text: The divergence of F = x²y i + y²z j + z²x k at the point (1, 2, 3) is ______
solution: Concept: ∇·F = ∂Fx/∂x + ∂Fy/∂y + ∂Fz/∂z (a scalar).
Exam tip: Divergence measures the net outflow per unit volume; a field with zero divergence everywhere is solenoidal (incompressible flow).

questions.text: The curl of the vector field F = y i − x j is
solution: Concept: ∇×F = (∂Fz/∂y − ∂Fy/∂z) i + (∂Fx/∂z − ∂Fz/∂x) j + (∂Fy/∂x − ∂Fx/∂y) k.
Only the k component survives: ∂(−x)/∂x − ∂(y)/∂y = −1 − 1 = −2
Exam tip: This field is a clockwise rigid rotation with angular velocity 1 rad/s; curl = 2 × angular velocity, here −2k.

questions.text: For twice continuously differentiable φ and F, which of the following is NOT identically zero?
solution: Concept: Two identities hold for all smooth fields: curl grad φ = 0 and div curl F = 0 (mixed partial derivatives cancel).
∇·(∇φ) = ∇²φ, the Laplacian, which is zero only for harmonic functions (e.g. φ = x² gives ∇²φ = 2).
Exam tip: Option (C) is zero too: it is div curl of the vector field φF.

questions.text: The vector field F = (x + 2y + az) i + (bx − 3y − z) j + (4x + cy + 2z) k is irrotational. The value of a + b + c is ______
solution: Concept: Irrotational means ∇×F = 0: all three components of the curl vanish.
i: ∂Fz/∂y − ∂Fy/∂z = c + 1 = 0 → c = −1
j: ∂Fx/∂z − ∂Fz/∂x = a − 4 = 0 → a = 4
Exam tip: An irrotational field is conservative (F = ∇φ) on a simply connected region.

questions.text: The work done by the force F = 3x² i + (2xz − y) j + z k in moving a particle along the straight line from (0, 0, 0) to (2, 1, 3) is ______
solution: Concept: W = ∫F·dr; parametrise the path and integrate in one variable.
Exam tip: This field is not conservative (∂Fy/∂x = 2z ≠ ∂Fx/∂y = 0), so the work depends on the path.

questions.text: The force F = (2xy + z³) i + x² j + 3xz² k moves a particle from (1, −2, 1) to (3, 1, 4). The work done is
solution: Concept: ∇×F = 0 here, so F = ∇φ and W = φ(end) − φ(start), whatever the path.
By inspection φ = x²y + xz³ (check: ∂φ/∂x = 2xy + z³, ∂φ/∂y = x², ∂φ/∂z = 3xz²)
Exam tip: Always test the curl first; a zero curl turns a long line integral into a one-line answer.

questions.text: Using Green's theorem, the value of ∮<sub>C</sub> [(3x − 8y²) dx + (4y − 6xy) dy], where C is the boundary of the triangle bounded by x = 0, y = 0 and x + y = 1 traversed anticlockwise (figure), is ______ (round off to two decimal places)
solution: Concept: Green's theorem: ∮(M dx + N dy) = ∬R(∂N/∂x − ∂M/∂y) dA for anticlockwise C.
Exam tip: Direct evaluation along the three sides gives the same 5/3, a good check if time permits.

questions.text: The outward flux of F = x³ i + y³ j + z³ k through the sphere x² + y² + z² = 1 (round off to two decimal places) is ______
solution: Concept: Gauss divergence theorem: ∯F·n dS = ∭∇·F dV.
∇·F = 3(x² + y² + z²) = 3r²
∭3r² dV = ∫01 3r² × 4πr² dr = 12π/5 = 7.54
Exam tip: Use spherical coordinates (dV = 4πr² dr for a radial integrand) whenever the divergence depends only on r.

questions.text: For F = −y i + x j, the circulation ∮F·dr around the circle x² + y² = 4 in the plane z = 0, traversed anticlockwise, is
solution: Concept: Stokes' theorem: ∮F·dr = ∬(∇×F)·n dS.
Circulation = 2 × 4π = 8π
Exam tip: Check directly: on r = 2, F·dr = r² dθ = 4 dθ, giving 8π over one turn.

questions.text: Using the line integral A = ½∮(x dy − y dx), the area enclosed by the ellipse x²/9 + y²/4 = 1 (round off to two decimal places) is ______
solution: Concept: Green's theorem with M = −y/2, N = x/2 gives ∂N/∂x − ∂M/∂y = 1, so the integral equals the area.
x = 3 cos θ, y = 2 sin θ: x dy − y dx = (6 cos²θ + 6 sin²θ) dθ = 6 dθ
Exam tip: ∮x dy and −∮y dx each also give the area on their own.

questions.text: The outward flux of F = x i + y j + z k through the surface of the cube 0 ≤ x, y, z ≤ 2 is ______
solution: Concept: Divergence theorem: flux = ∭∇·F dV.
Exam tip: For the position vector r, the flux through any closed surface is 3 × the enclosed volume.

questions.text: With r = xi + yj + zk and r = |r| ≠ 0, ∇²(rn) = n(n + 1)rn−2. Among the options, rn is harmonic (∇²rn = 0) for
solution: Concept: ∇²(rn) = n(n + 1) rn−2 vanishes for n = 0 or n = −1.
So 1/r is harmonic away from the origin: it is the potential of a point source (or a point mass/charge).
Exam tip: Related results: ∇rn = n rn−2r, ∇·r = 3 and ∇×r = 0.
